decisions.reason: As a close-to-core carpet with modest carrying costs, it remains a low-cost option and its continued presence suggests no clear evidence of failure yet.
The premium hand-knotted carpet is niche but supports the firm's design-led positioning, so management would keep the option open while demand continues to clarify.
The corner bench is more usage-specific and therefore somewhat more exposed to pruning, but it still builds on established capabilities and is not weak enough to abandon now.
This carpet still faces the greatest overlap risk in the portfolio, yet after Product C was removed the remaining learning value and limited cost still justify keeping it for now.
The swivel shell chair line fits the firm's push into flexible workplace concepts and appears strategically strong enough to retain as market feedback matures.
